title: kv-occupancy-aware-retention-and-stochastic-evictor
author: Asha Rao
description:
Motivation: large multi-tenant workloads expose two correlated but under-optimized behaviors in our KV cache: uneven occupancy causing high fragmentation, and eviction churn under transient load spikes. This PR introduces an occupancy-aware retention layer plus a stochastic, bounded-sample evictor that aims to reduce fragmentation, smooth eviction pressure during bursts, and preserve hot prefixes without heavy global compaction.

Summary of changes and rationale: implement a lightweight occupancy bucketing scheme that tracks hotness at segment granularity, add a lease-like soft-retention token to avoid immediately evicting recently-resurrected keys, and replace the deterministic LRU-scan used by the existing evictor with a probabilistic sampler that prioritizes underfilled buckets and respects per-tenant soft-quotas. The new algorithm reduces large contiguous free/used alternations, lowering fragmentation-induced memory amplification. We also add a cooperative compact hint channel so tenants can trigger low-priority compaction during idle cycles (scheduler-integrated).

Checklist: - [x] Core algorithm implemented (kv/retention + kv/evictor) - [x] Unit tests for eviction invariants and lease expiry - [x] Microbenchmarks (local and CI perf job) - [x] Node-level scheduler integration for low-priority compaction hints - [x] Documentation and rollout config flags

Operational notes: rollout gated behind feature flag KV_OCCUPANCY_RETENTION. Default is off for clusters < 8 GPUs to avoid unintended interactions with small-node packing heuristics. Telemetry exposes: eviction_cycles, sampled_bucket_hit_rate, retention_leases_active, tenant_eviction_pressure. Guidance: enable on a canary tenant first; monitor sampled_bucket_hit_rate and retention_leases_active to tune bucket granularity (default 128 slots).

Why different from previous work: unlike pure compaction or spill strategies, this approach focuses on reducing fragmentation at allocation-time by steering retention policy with occupancy signals and a low-cpu probabilistic evictor instead of expensive global scans or synchronous spill-to-disk paths. It complements, rather than replaces, the existing spill/overflow mechanisms.

Links: Linear ENG-2201 (design), supporting perf run artifacts: ci/perf/kv-occupancy-2025-11-18, internal doc: docs/kv-occupancy-retention.md

review_thread: Diego Morales: The probabilistic sampler looks promising; can you quantify worst-case memory growth during a sudden spike?
Asha Rao: Added a burst-bound parameter (max_retention_leases) and a backoff path that forces immediate sampling under emergency pressure. See retention.rs:burst_control().
Priya Singh: Please add tenant isolation tests (one noisy tenant shouldn't evict another's retained keys).
Asha Rao: Added tenancy isolation unit tests and an integration scenario that simulates cross-tenant pressure. CI integration-tests included; added tenant_eviction_pressure metric.
Evan Li: Performance numbers look good but the integration test flaked once; can we stabilize the perf job?
Asha Rao: Tightened test timings and added deterministic seeds for sampler on CI. Re-ran perf job; results stable.
benchmarks: micro: under sustained 256-token workload, mean memory usage -18% compared to baseline
throughput: +6% under 8x concurrent streams due to reduced eviction blocking
eviction-churn: -42% measured as fewer reclaims per-minute in same workload
fragmentation-index: -35% measured by contiguous free-run length distribution
release_notes: Introduce occupancy-aware retention and a probabilistic evictor to reduce KV cache fragmentation and eviction churn.
Feature flag: KV_OCCUPANCY_RETENTION (off by default for small clusters).
Recommended rollout: canary on a tenant and monitor eviction_churn and p99 latency before enabling org-wide.
